name: Relevance of patient-level detection of causative pathogens in blood against the final clinical diagnosis (Huang et al. 2026 Table 2) to "Select a DNA pathogen-identification workflow for diagnostic testing"
description: Two DNA sequencing workflows on blood (targeted probe-capture bstNGS and untargeted mNGS) and two conventional tests are scored on the same 122 patients against an adjudicated clinical diagnosis, which bears directly on the use case's question of which DNA workflow detects clinically relevant pathogens from blood. It is proxy evidence: the reference incorporates NGS results, the cohort is retrospective, the specimens are plasma microbial cell-free DNA in pneumonia-associated sepsis, and the targeted assay detects only its 1,872-organism panel.

attributes.endpoint: Patient-level sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and accuracy (95% intervals) of blood bstNGS, blood mNGS, conventional tests and blood culture against the adjudicated clinical diagnosis in 122 ICU patients, overall and for gram-positive, gram-negative and fungal pneumonia
attributes.rationale: Two DNA sequencing workflows on blood (targeted probe-capture bstNGS and untargeted mNGS) and two conventional tests are scored on the same 122 patients against an adjudicated clinical diagnosis, which bears directly on the use case's question of which DNA workflow detects clinically relevant pathogens from blood. It is proxy evidence: the reference incorporates NGS results, the cohort is retrospective, the specimens are plasma microbial cell-free DNA in pneumonia-associated sepsis, and the targeted assay detects only its 1,872-organism panel.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator and preserved limitations before citing a result.
Do not combine these results with another protocol's results; reference standards, specimens and scoring units differ between sources.
limitations: Incorporation bias: the reference was established primarily from BALF mNGS and CMT results (Methods 'Sample enrollment and standard-of-care microbiology testing' paragraph 3; Table 2 footnote), with clinical adjudication. CMTs is scored against a reference that contains it, which favours CMTs, and BALF mNGS is a sequencing assay on a different specimen.
Retrospective single-centre cohort; 61 of 183 screened patients excluded.
Few patients are reference-negative: the count is not printed, and the specificity intervals are wide (44.44% for bstNGS, 24.56% to 66.28%).
Targeted panel: bstNGS cannot detect organisms outside its 1,872 probes, which bears on the use case's question of organisms absent from the reference.
Blood culture PPV in fungal pneumonia is printed 0.00% with a zero denominator (result source_anomaly).
Commercial assay with two co-authors from its supplier (Geneplus-Beijing); no competing interests declared.
